name: United Arab Emirates
headline: United Arab Emirates: +6.2% growth in 2025, 1.3% inflation, debt 34% of GDP
sections: United Arab Emirates is a $614 billion economy (2025), the world's 28th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +6.2% in 2025, faster than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $79K at purchasing-power parity (2024), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 9.4% of GDP (2024).
Consumer prices rose 1.3% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges, down from 4.8% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 2.2% (2025), below the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 6.5% (2025).
Gross government debt is 34% of GDP (2025), a low level that has risen from 30% in 2020. The general government balance is +3.9% of GDP (2025), a surplus.
The current account balance is +13.3% of GDP (2025), a large surplus. Trade equals 199% of GDP (2023), a highly open economy. Net FDI inflows were 8.3% of GDP (2024).
IMF projections put government debt at 26% of GDP by 2031, on a declining path from today's level. Life expectancy is 83.1 years (2024). Population: 11.3 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
